title: Outcome Disclosure and Temporal Refinement in Multi-Battle Team Contests
abstract: arXiv:2608.22694v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A team-contest designer values output rather than expenditure; nonlinear conversion makes the distinction consequential. We study two non-pecuniary instruments in majority-rule contests decided by pairwise all-pay battles with private abilities: disclosing resolved outcomes and splitting the battle schedule into finer blocks. Neither changes a battle's average pivotality; each only redistributes it across histories. Under nested information structures, this redistribution makes equilibrium ability-scaled expenditure weakly more dispersed player by player without changing its mean; expected aggregate expenditure is invariant across all designs considered. The resulting convex-order comparison ranks expected total output: convex output costs favor no disclosure and coarser temporal structures, concave costs favor full disclosure and finer ones, and linear costs make both comparisons neutral. The rankings hold for finite-support and smooth

translated_title: 多战役团队竞赛中的结果披露与时间细化
translated_abstract: 团队竞赛的设计者重视产出而非支出；非线性转换使得这种区别具有重要意义。我们研究了多数规则竞赛中的两种非货币工具，该竞赛由两两全付战役决定，且参与者具有私人能力：披露已解决的结果，以及将战役时间表细分为更细的块。两者都不会改变战役的平均关键性；它们仅将其重新分配在不同的历史路径上。在嵌套信息结构下，这种重新分配使得均衡能力调整后的支出在逐玩家基础上弱更分散，而不改变其均值；在所有考虑的设计中，预期总支出保持不变。由此产生的凸序比较排名预期总产出：凸产出成本偏好不披露和更粗的时间结构，凹成本偏好完全披露和更细的结构，而线性成本使两种比较均中性。该排名适用于有限支撑和光滑分布。
tldr: 本文发现，在团队竞赛中，披露结果和细化时间安排不改变预期总支出，但通过重新分配关键性影响产出，其效果取决于产出成本函数的凹凸性。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that in team contests, outcome disclosure and temporal refinement do not alter expected total expenditure but affect output by redistributing pivotality, with effects depending on the convexity or concavity of output costs.
